evidence.quote: **Current behaviour:** observed-in-code. A classifier panic can be treated as a request failure. A trip-policy panic during regular accounting may count the failure twice because Execute recovers and attempts accounting again after unlock. A notification panic during panic accounting can replace the request panic after state has committed. Panics during admission bypass Execute recovery. gobreaker.go:229 ("generation, err := cb.beforeRequest()"). gobreaker.go:234 ("defer func() {"). gobreaker.go:237 ("cb.afterRequest(generation, false)"). gobreaker.go:238 ("panic(e)"). gobreaker.go:243 ("cb.afterRequest(generation, cb.isSuccessful(err))"). gobreaker.go:295 ("defer cb.mutex.Unlock()"). gobreaker.go:325 ("cb.counts.onFailure()"). gobreaker.go:354 ("cb.state = state"). gobreaker.go:359 ("cb.onStateChange(cb.name, prev, state)").

- Normal return, input panic, policy panic, same-thread callback reentry, blocked request and Goexit have distinct failure outcomes. Execute only registers recovery after successful admission; the recovery scope includes classifier and accounting. Failure accounting can itself panic before the original panic is rethrown. No system retry of request work. observed-in-code gobreaker.go:229 ("generation, err := cb.beforeRequest()"). gobreaker.go:234 ("defer func() {"). gobreaker.go:235 ("e := recover()"). gobreaker.go:237 ("cb.afterRequest(generation, false)"). gobreaker.go:238 ("panic(e)"). gobreaker.go:295 ("defer cb.mutex.Unlock()").
